findings.claim: Chords measured between physical markers on a cylindrical part follow the cos^4(alpha)/(24 R^2) coefficient

hypothesis: On a cylinder of radius R, the geodesic at angle alpha from the circumferential direction has chord deficit s - c = cos^4(alpha) s^3/(24 R^2) + O(s^5): largest circumferentially, zero on rulings, although the Gaussian curvature is zero everywhere.
input_data: 40 geometric samples s in R*[0.02, 0.3]; 60-step RK4 geodesics over s in [0, 0.3R]
mathematical_model: Helix X(s) = (R cos(s cos(a)/R), R sin(s cos(a)/R), s sin(a)); kappa = cos^2(a)/R, tau = sin(a) cos(a)/R; c^2 = (2R sin(s cos(a)/2R))^2 + (s sin(a))^2 = s^2 - cos^4(a) s^4/(12R^2) + cos^6(a) s^6/(360 R^4) + O(s^8).
numerical_result: max normalized fit error 6.7e-12; integrated chord error 6.0e-15 R; circumferential coefficient 0.041666666667 (1/24 = 0.041666666667); ruling max |s - c| over s > 0 2.8e-16 R; the sympy series comparison (symbolic residuals), when sympy is available, is recorded on the derivation finding (independent_check).
observation_model: Noise-free chords of embedded points; no instrument.
